The words

Children of the Heavenly King,
As ye journey, sweetly sing;
Sing your Saviour's worthy praise,
Glorious in his works and ways.

Ye are travelling home to God,
In the way the fathers trod;
They are happy now, and ye
Soon their happiness shall see.

Shout, ye little flock, and blest;
You on Jesus' throne shall rest;
There your seat is now prepared,
There your kingdom and reward.

Lord, submissive make us go,
Ready, leaving all below;
Only thou our Leader be,
And we still will follow thee.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Ab and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on d (A♭).
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

John Cennick wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 379 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Christian rejoicing in Hope”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BEES; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.

  • Words: John Cennick (1718–1755)
  • Music (1862): John Bacchus Dykes (1823–1876)

Tune ST. BEES by John Bacchus Dykes (1823–1876); words by John Cennick (1718–1755).

Deliver; Thou Canst Save, Nay, I Cannot Let Thee Go, Now May Fervent Prayer Arise, Partners of a Glorious Hope, There's a Strife We All Must Wage, What a Mournful Life Is Mine, While the Stars Unnumbered Roll.

Questions about Children of the Heavenly King

What is the doh of Children of the Heavenly King?

In this version, in Ab major, doh is Ab. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Children of the Heavenly King start on?

It starts on d (A♭ in Ab major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

Is Children of the Heavenly King in the public domain?

Yes. John Cennick died in 1755, John Bacchus Dykes died in 1876; the words were in print by 1853 and the music in 1862. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
